concerns.text: T015-llm describes a logic that loads pre-existing files and falls back only if the *file* is missing. This violates FR-002 which mandates the system MUST automatically fall back if LLM *generation fails* (timeout/empty) during execution. The task lacks the mechanism to attempt real-time inference and catch runtime errors to trigger the fallback in 'Real' mode.

T015-real (Real Data Collection) does not explicitly include the step to invoke the LatencyCalibrator (T012) or ensure the startup gate (T012a) is active. FR-003 requires a local loopback latency test at startup to verify ≤100ms precision before recording data. Omitting this verification step in the real study task violates the requirement.

T000 documents a 'Scope Reduction' from 'Human Subject Study' to 'Deterministic Simulation' for CI. While simulation for CI is valid, the task text frames this as a replacement for the real study in the documentation artifact, creating a semantic drift that contradicts FR-001 and FR-003 which require the system to support a real study with real participants. The spec does not authorize a permanent scope reduction of the study itself.

T024-stats includes implementing 'Top-K accuracy' metrics. The spec's Success Criteria (SC-001, SC-002) and User Story 2 only define 'Correct-first-line identification rate' (accuracy) and 'time-to-decision' (speed). Adding Top-K metrics is unrequested scope creep that has no corresponding requirement or success criterion to verify against, violating the constraint that tasks must not introduce features not demanded by the spec.
